title: Extending Rademacher Complexity-Based Generalization Theory to Domain Generalization
abstract: arXiv:2611.25650v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Domain generalization (DG) aims to train models on multiple source domains with distinct distributions to ensure robust performance on unseen target domains. In doing so, it elevates the concept of generalization from the traditional sample level to the distribution level. Existing theoretical frameworks introduce a domain space endowed with a meta-distribution to extend classical generalization analysis to this new setting. However, these approaches typically treat the domain space as devoid of geometry. In reality, the domain space is an inherently infinite-dimensional, nonlinear abstract space composed of probability distributions, and its complex geometric properties fundamentally determine generalization behavior. Consequently, existing geometry-free theories of domain generalization have a fundamental limitation. translated_title: 将基于Rademacher复杂度的泛化理论扩展到领域泛化
translated_abstract: 领域泛化（DG）旨在让模型在多个具有不同分布的源领域上进行训练，以确保其在未见过的目标领域上具有稳健的性能。在此过程中，它将泛化的概念从传统的样本层面提升到了分布层面。现有的理论框架通过引入一个赋予元分布的领域空间，将经典的泛化分析扩展到这一新设定。然而，这些方法通常将领域空间视为没有几何结构的。实际上，领域空间本质上是一个由概率分布组成的无限维、非线性抽象空间，其复杂的几何性质从根本上决定了泛化行为。因此，现有的无几何结构的领域泛化理论存在根本性局限：它们缺乏对分布层面泛化与样本层面泛化之间区别的形式化刻画。
tldr: 本文将基于Rademacher复杂度的经典泛化理论扩展到领域泛化设定，通过考虑由概率分布构成的领域空间的几何性质，弥补了现有无几何理论无法形式化刻画分布层面泛化与样本层面泛化区别的根本局限。
en_tdlr: This paper extends Rademacher complexity-based generalization theory to domain generalization by incorporating the geometric properties of the probability-distribution domain space, addressing the fundamental limitation of existing geometry-free theories in formally characterizing the distinction between distribution-level and sample-level generalization.
